user_input: What are the requirements for a therapeutic radiation machine treatment room operating above 500 kV?
reference: All protective barriers must be fixed except for access doors to the treatment room or movable beam interceptors, the control panel must be located outside the treatment room, and adequate shielding must be provided.

user_input: What facility and equipment diagrams must applicants submit for rooms where radioactive materials are used?
reference: Applicants must describe assigned areas for receipt, storage, preparation, and measurement of radioactive materials and submit scale diagrams showing shielding locations, proximity to unrestricted areas, and ventilation schematics if materials may become airborne.

user_input: What are the four main types of ionizing radiation discussed in basic health physics?
reference: The four main types of radiation dealt with in health physics are alpha particles, beta particles, gamma and X rays (counted as one type), and neutrons.

user_input: What is NRC Form 540 used for in low-level radioactive waste shipping?
reference: NRC Form 540 is the Uniform Low-Level Radioactive Waste Manifest shipping paper used to document shipper, collector, and waste shipment details.

user_input: What are the Container Description Codes and structural overpack (-OP) rules on NRC Form 541?
reference: On NRC Form 541, Container Description Codes for containers or waste requiring disposal in approved structural overpacks must have the numerical code followed by -OP.

user_input: What is NRC Form 542 used for on the Uniform Low-Level Radioactive Waste Manifest?
reference: NRC Form 542 is the Manifest Index and Regional Compact Tabulation form of the Uniform Low-Level Radioactive Waste Manifest.

user_input: What does NRC Regulatory Issue Summary 2004-17 say about revised decay-in-storage provisions for radioactive waste?
reference: NRC Regulatory Issue Summary 2004-17, Revision 1 addresses revised decay-in-storage provisions for storing radioactive waste containing byproduct material.

user_input: What does NRC Information Notice 94-07 state about solubility criteria for liquid effluent releases to sanitary sewerage?
reference: NRC Information Notice 94-07 addresses solubility criteria under 10 CFR 20.2003(a)(1) for liquid effluent releases to sanitary sewerage, noting that formal solubilities below 0.003 mole/liter indicate compounds not readily soluble.

user_input: What does NRC Information Notice 99-33 advise medical licensees regarding landfills and medical waste incinerators?
reference: NRC Information Notice 99-33 advises NRC medical licensees that operators of most landfills and medical waste incinerators are not licensed to manage low-level radioactive materials.

user_input: What does RIS 2008-12 state regarding extended radioactive waste storage versus disposal?
reference: NRC RIS 2008-12 on extended low-level radioactive waste storage emphasizes that storage is not a substitute for disposal.

user_input: What is the purpose of Regulatory Guide 1.86 regarding termination of operating licenses for nuclear reactors?
reference: Regulatory Guide 1.86 covers reactor license termination, requiring remaining radioactive materials to be isolated by physical barriers and a comprehensive radiation survey prior to release for unrestricted use.

user_input: How must records of dose to an embryo or fetus be maintained according to Regulatory Guide 8.13?
reference: Under Regulatory Guide 8.13 on prenatal radiation exposure, records of dose to an embryo or fetus if monitoring was required must be kept with the records of dose to the declared pregnant woman.

category: Sec 080 - External Dosimetry_External Radiation Protection & Shielding
user_input: When must licensees provide additional dosimeters according to NRC Regulatory Guide 8.40?
reference: NRC Regulatory Guide 8.40 notes licensees will most likely need additional dosimeters when 10 CFR 20.1502 requires individual monitoring and references ICRP Publication 26 tissue weighting factors.

user_input: What does Regulatory Guide 4.22 address regarding decommissioning planning during operations under 10 CFR Part 20 Subpart E?
reference: Regulatory Guide 4.22 addresses decommissioning planning under 10 CFR Part 20 Subpart E, providing guidance to design facilities and procedures to minimize waste generation and facility contamination.

user_input: What information is reported on NRC Form 653 under 10 CFR 32 for industrial device transfers?
reference: NRC Form 653 under 10 CFR 32 is the Transfers of Industrial Devices Report to General Licensees, capturing vendor, license number, reporting period, and general licensee location details.

user_input: What is NRC Form 313A (AMP) under 10 CFR 35.51 used to document?
reference: NRC Form 313A (AMP) under 10 CFR 35.51 documents Authorized Medical Physicist training and experience and includes the preceptor attestation.

user_input: What did the GAO-12-925 report find about security of high-risk radiological sources at U.S. medical facilities?
reference: GAO-12-925 examined radiological source security at U.S. medical facilities, finding NRC requirements and implementation did not ensure security of high-risk sources and describing NNSA security upgrades.

user_input: What components must be included in a hazardous materials transportation security plan under Enhanced Security Requirements?
reference: A transportation security plan must include company security objectives, specific security procedures, employee responsibilities, actions to take in a security breach, and organizational security structure.

user_input: Within how many days must a shipping licensee submit a written report for lost or missing Category 2 radioactive material under RIS 2015-03?
reference: Under RIS 2015-03 and 10 CFR 37.81(g), a shipping licensee must submit a written report to the NRC within 30 days of an initial report of lost, missing, or diverted Category 2 quantities of radioactive material.

user_input: What does NUREG-2155 provide guidance on regarding 10 CFR Part 37?
expected_file: NUREG-2155 Implementation Guidance for 10 CFR part 37.pdf
reference: NUREG-2155 provides implementation guidance for 10 CFR Part 37 on physical protection of Category 1 and Category 2 quantities of radioactive material, including Subpart D transport and import/export scope.

user_input: How do SSRCR Part A General Provisions define airborne radioactive material and bioassay?
reference: SSRCR Part A defines airborne radioactive material as radioactive material dispersed in air as dusts, fumes, particulates, mists, vapors, or gases, and bioassay as determining radioactive material in the human body.

user_input: What must be submitted prior to construction for radiation machine shielding plan review under SSRCR Part B Sec. B.4?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part B_Registration of Radiation Machine Facilities and Services.pdf
reference: Under SSRCR Part B Sec. B.4, prior to construction, the floor plans, shielding specifications, and equipment arrangement of new installations must be submitted for shielding plan review.

user_input: What does SSRCR Part D Sec. D.1101 require regarding radiation protection programs?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part D_Standards for Protection Against Radiation.pdf
reference: Under SSRCR Part D Sec. D.1101, each licensee or registrant must develop, document, and implement a radiation protection program sufficient to ensure compliance with D.2102 recordkeeping requirements.

user_input: How does SSRCR Part F define heat unit and image intensifier in diagnostic x-ray systems?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part F_Use of X-rays in the Healing Arts.pdf
reference: SSRCR Part F defines a heat unit as the product of kVp x mA x second, and an image intensifier as a device that instantaneously converts an x-ray pattern into a corresponding light image of higher intensity.

user_input: What warning wording is required near an analytical x-ray tube energizing switch under SSRCR Part H?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part H_Radiation Safety Requirements for Analytical X-ray Equipment.pdf
reference: SSRCR Part H requires the warning CAUTION RADIATION - THIS EQUIPMENT PRODUCES RADIATION WHEN ENERGIZED or similar wording near any switch that energizes an x-ray tube.

user_input: What site and waste descriptions are required in a land disposal facility application under SSRCR Part M?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part M_Licensing Requirements for Land Disposal of Radioactive Waste.pdf
reference: SSRCR Part M requires a description of the proposed disposal site location, general character of activities, types and quantities of waste to be received and disposed of, other land uses, and proposed facilities and equipment.

user_input: What is the annual public dose limit for operations involving TENORM under SSRCR Part N Sec. N.5?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part N_Regulations and Licensing of TENORM.pdf
reference: Under SSRCR Part N Sec. N.5, persons licensed under N.10 or N.20 must conduct TENORM operations so members of the public do not exceed 1 millisievert (0.1 rem) TEDE annually.

user_input: What descriptions and diagrams must an irradiator license application include under SSRCR Part Q?
expected_file: SSRCR_Part Q_Licensing and Radiation Safety Requirements for Irradiators.pdf
reference: Under SSRCR Part Q, an irradiator application must describe access control systems (Q.9), radiation monitors (Q.12), leak detection methods and sensitivity (Q.23), and include a diagram showing all interlocks and monitors.

user_input: What are the non-fixed surface contamination limits averaged over 300 cm2 under SSRCR Part T?
reference: Under SSRCR Part T, non-fixed contamination on an accessible surface averaged over 300 cm2 must not exceed 4 Bq/cm2 (10^-4 uCi/cm2) for beta, gamma, and low-toxicity alpha emitters, or 0.4 Bq/cm2 (10^-5 uCi/cm2) for all other alpha emitters.

user_input: What does RIS 2002-06 state about deep dose equivalent (DDE) assignment and protective apparel in medical x-ray exposure?
reference: RIS 2002-06 requires assigned deep dose equivalent (DDE) for the highest exposed part of the body and describes acceptable alternative methods for medical x-ray exposure when a protective apron is worn.

user_input: Which particle did Chadwick identify as having no electrical charge and roughly the same mass as a proton?
reference: He discovered an uncharged particle with roughly the same mass as a proton, called the neutron, which is contained in the atomic nucleus.

user_input: Who is credited with discovering natural radioactivity while working with uranium salts and photographic plates?
reference: Henri Becquerel is credited with discovering natural radioactivity in 1896 while working with uranium salts and photographic plates.

user_input: What is the SI unit and special name for absorbed dose, and how does it relate to J/kg?
reference: The SI unit for absorbed dose is J/kg, given the special name gray (Gy) where 1 Gy = 1 J/kg.

user_input: What is the EPA indoor radon guideline cited in The Source of Radon Risk Perceptions?
expected_file: The Source of Radon Risk Perceptions.pdf
reference: The Source of Radon Risk Perceptions cites the EPA indoor radon guideline of 4 pCi/L.

user_input: Which CFR rule grants Agreement State licensees reciprocal recognition to work in non-Agreement States according to NUREG-1556 Vol. 19?
reference: 10 CFR 150.20 grants Agreement State licensees a general license to conduct licensed activities in non-Agreement States under reciprocal recognition via NRC Form 241.

user_input: Where must shipping documents (papers) be kept during road and rail hazardous materials transport according to ERG2012?
reference: According to ERG2012, shipping documents (papers) are kept in the cab of a motor vehicle for road transport and with the crew/locomotive for rail transport.
